# GS1 Data

This record covers the `FeatherQR.Gs1` package: GS1's carriers in the QR family, the application identifier (AI) table generated from the GS1 Barcode Syntax Dictionary and how it is kept current, the checks the GS1 General Specifications define, `(AI)` text and GS1 Digital Link URIs in both directions, the read after a decode, and the GS1 entry points the package adds to the Standard QR and rMQR generators. The bit stream below it, FNC1 in first and second position and the `%` rule, is in [standardqr-encoder.md](standardqr-encoder.md) and [rmqr-encoder.md](rmqr-encoder.md) (FNC1) and the two decoder records. Why the layer is a package of its own, and its place in the package graph, are in [qrcode-symbologies.md](qrcode-symbologies.md) (Package architecture, Why four packages under a new name). Its oracles and its fixture corpus are in [qrcode-test-fixtures.md](qrcode-test-fixtures.md). The README's GS1 section is the user's guide.

## What

### GS1's carriers in the QR family

GS1 uses two QR carriers, and they need different things. The rules below are from the General Specifications Release 26.0, the Digital Link URI Syntax 1.7.0 and the 2D Barcodes at Retail POS Implementation Guideline 1.1.0, read on 2026-10-10. The General Specifications were read through GS1 Portugal's copy of the PDF, whose identity with the official file was not confirmed.

- GS1 QR Code carries an element string behind FNC1 in first position and is transmitted as `]Q3` (5.7, Table 5-2). It serves healthcare, logistics, assets, tobacco, direct part marking, AI (8200) and internal applications, and it is not a retail point-of-sale option. ECI and Structured Append are not supported in it (5.7.3), and neither is Kanji mode (5.7.2). A separator is written as GS or `%` and always transmitted as GS (7.8.4). The quiet zone is 4X on every side (5.7.4.2), which is Standard QR's default here.
- QR Code with a Digital Link URI is plain QR with no FNC1, transmitted as `]Q1` (5.10). It is the retail carrier. GS1's 2D migration at the point of sale lists it with GS1 DataMatrix and Data Matrix with a Digital Link URI (8.2, Table 8-1), and the retail guideline sets the end of 2027 as a goal, not a mandate. At retail the URI is uncompressed (GSCN 22-309).
- Micro QR is "not supported in the GS1 system" (5.7.1). rMQR is not a GS1 carrier: Release 26.0 has no occurrence of rMQR or ISO/IEC 23941, and the GSCN index of 2013 to 2026 has no entry for it.

GS1 data is ASCII (CSET 82, 39 and 64, 7.11). With `EciMode.Default` the encoders write no ECI header for ASCII text and never write Kanji mode for it, and a Structured Append set refuses any FNC1 mode. So an element string encoded with FNC1 in first position and default options is a compliant GS1 QR Code, and only an `EciMode` the caller names breaks that. The suite holds the property on every symbol `CreateGs1` writes for the GS1 corpus, so no member refuses an option for it.

### The data layer

The element string, with U+001D as the separator, is the hub. Every conversion is one hop to or from it, and it is the form the FNC1 encoder takes and the decoders return. A Digital Link URI goes into a symbol as plain text.

```text
(AI) text ── FromHri ──┐                       ┌── ToHri ──> (AI) text
                       ▼                       │
DL URI ── FromDigitalLink ──> element string (GS as U+001D) ── ToDigitalLink ──> DL URI
                                  │           ▲
              Fnc1 = FirstPosition│           │ info.Fnc1.IsFirstPosition
                                  ▼           │
                QRCodeGenerator / RmQRCodeGenerator / decoders
```

| Member | From and to | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| `TryFromHri` | `(AI)` text to an element string | every check, pairings included |
| `TryToDigitalLink` | an element string to a URI, under an optional stem | every check, pairings included, and what a URI can carry |
| `TryToHri` | an element string to `(AI)` text | what splitting needs, unknown AIs read |
| `TryFromDigitalLink` | a URI to an element string | what reading needs: the URI's structure, and what the element string needs to split back into the same elements |
| `TryValidate` | an element string | every check |
| `EnumerateElements` | an element string to its AIs and values as spans | what splitting needs |
| `TryRead` | a decoder's text and its `Fnc1Mode` to `(AI)` text | what reading needs |
| `CreateGs1`, `CreateGs1DigitalLink` | `(AI)` text or an element string to a symbol | every check, pairings included |

- The AI table is generated from the GS1 Barcode Syntax Dictionary, release 2026-01-27, committed with its license and provenance under the test fixtures, by a test that fails on drift and rewrites outside CI. It is byte span data with no allocation and no static constructor, about 7.5 KB. The dictionary is Apache-2.0, so the package carries `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` and the core packages carry nothing. Two tables of the General Specifications that it declares frozen are hand-coded and cross-checked against the dictionary by tests: AI length by the first two digits (Table 7-5) and the predefined element string lengths (Table 7-6).
- The 34 linters the dictionary names are implemented in managed code from the rules of the General Specifications and the standards they cite, and each is held to the reference linters' own unit tests, imported with the dictionary (5,656 vectors). Three rules were read off the oracle where the text leaves them open: an IBAN's country code is an ISO 3166 alpha-2 code, CSET 64 padding is one or two `=` that bring the length to a multiple of three, and an empty value passes the no-zero-prefix rule. The ISO 3166, ISO 4217, media type and package type lists are not in the dictionary file. They come from the reference linters' sources at the same tag, committed beside the dictionary.
- One split serves every reader and check (`Gs1ElementString.EnumerateElements`, `TryValidate`, and the conversions). An AI's length comes from its first two digits, so an AI newer than the table is still read. Only an element string of predefined length (Table 7-6) is read by its length, and it is whether the table knows the AI or not, since that table is frozen: a newer AI under prefixes 31 to 36 or 41 is encoded with no separator after it, and a reader that ran to the separator would swallow the element after it (found in the review before the pull request, the Syntax Engine reads it the same way). A separator inside the window cuts the value short rather than becoming part of it. Every other value, a fixed-length format such as (8005) included, runs to the next separator and has its length checked after, because the General Specifications require a separator after it (7.8.6.2) and a reader that took the format's length would pass a missing separator in silence. One separator after any value is consumed whether or not the AI needed it (7.8.6.3). A separator at the start or two in a row are refused.
- `TryValidate` runs every check in the order the Syntax Engine runs its validations: each element's components (lengths, character set, linters), then every exclusion, then every requisite, then a repeated AI with another value, then the engine's one rule beside the dictionary's pairings, that a digital signature (8030) signs a serialised key, so (253), (255) and (8003) must carry their optional serial component when (8030) is present whichever requisite alternative let it in. It agrees with the engine's verdict on every comparable fixture of the GS1 corpus. The first build read the serial rule into the dictionary's `+` requisite alternatives, which gave the same verdict only when the key was the sole satisfier, and the review before the pull request made it the engine's separate pass.
- The rules between elements take time in proportion to the length of the text and allocate nothing. They ask a set of the AIs present, kept on the stack. Rules that scanned the text for each element took the square of the element count, and the entry points made that reachable from the generators for text of any length.
- Two-digit years resolve to the century that puts them within -49 to +50 years of the current year (7.12), from the clock. The reference linter compiles a fixed pivot year instead. The two agree on every vector until 2050, when a YY of 00 leaves the window and 29 February 2000 stops being a date for this library.
- `Gs1Error` is a kind with an offset and a length into the input, and `Gs1ErrorKind` has 21 members chosen so that each names a different repair. A linter failure maps to one of three: a check digit, a date or time, or another rule of the AI.
- The (AI) text form (`TryToHri`, `TryFromHri`, their span forms and length twins) is `(AI)value` pairs with nothing between them, a literal `(` in a value written `\(`, a `\` written `\\` (no GS1 character set holds one, but a decoded symbol can, and unescaped it would let a value run into the next pair when the text is read back), and no blank after the closing parenthesis, although GS1's HRI style allows one and the Syntax Engine prints one: a blank is an invalid character in the value. Formatting runs the split and nothing else, so an element string `TryValidate` refuses can still be shown. Building runs every check and places the separators where the General Specifications require one (7.8), after every element but the last unless its AI is of predefined length, and never reorders the elements. Its errors point into the text the caller gave, escapes included, and a pairing error names the whole pair. A short destination is reported only for data that passes, so the caller sees the data's fault first. zxing-cpp's `TextMode.HRI`, the fixtures' other (AI) text, falls back to the raw element string, or keeps a raw separator inside the text, where its own table could not split, so it is compared only where it produced (AI) text.
- The Digital Link form (`TryToDigitalLink`, `TryFromDigitalLink`, their span forms and length twins) is URI Syntax 1.7.0, uncompressed. Building runs every check and writes the canonical form: the first primary key leads, its qualifier sequence is the one that matches the most elements among those that leave only data attributes for the query, the query is in the lexical order of the AIs with each AI once, and the stem is `https://id.gs1.org` unless one is given (a stem that is not an http or https prefix throws, as a malformed option does). Reading takes any stem and follows the Syntax Engine's parser: the key is found from the end of the path, numeric query keys are AIs and an unknown one is refused, other keys are ignored. An AI that appears twice in a URI is refused even with equal values, as the engine refuses it. Four departures from the engine are held by tests and listed in [qrcode-test-fixtures.md](qrcode-test-fixtures.md): the scheme is case-insensitive, a short GTIN is not padded, a malformed escape is refused, and (01)(235)(10) builds as `/01/…/235/…?10=…` where the engine strands (235). Reading checks the structure plus what the element string needs to split back into the same elements, a predefined-length value's length and that no escape decodes to a control character, and leaves every other check on a value to `TryValidate`. The table decides which AIs a URI may carry, so (7041) and (8040) to (8043), which URI Syntax 1.7.0 lists and dictionary 2026-01-27 does not flag, are refused until a release flags them. A compressed URI is refused by a heuristic on its last path segment, since the frozen compression is not read.
- `TryRead` is the decode side's one entry: a decoder's text with its `Fnc1Mode` gives the (AI) text, from the element string under FNC1 in first position and from the Digital Link URI otherwise, so no decoder gained a GS1 member. It checks only what reading needs, so an element string with a wrong check digit still reads, and a view that presents the data as GS1 data runs `TryValidate` beside it.
- Everything on the data layer is `Try`: nothing throws for its input, which a fuzz test holds over every conversion and the read, and the span forms allocate nothing, which a Release-only test holds. Each conversion returns a string or writes into the caller's span, and each span form has a `TryGet…Length` twin that gives the exact length after the same checks.

### The dictionary and its updates

- `Gs1ElementString.DictionaryRelease` names the release the table came from, so a caller refused with `UnknownAi` on building can tell an AI newer than the package from a typo. The design is closed to a dictionary release in every other respect: AIs, flags, pairings, qualifier sequences and code lists are generated data, a new or renamed linter or a changed file syntax stops the generator or the parser instead of passing in silence, and the reference vectors imported with the dictionary make a changed rule red before the code follows. The steps of an update are in the header of `tools/get_gs1_syntax_engine.cs`, beside the pins they change. The table is compiled in by design, and no member takes a dictionary at run time: a caller-supplied dictionary would decide what the library accepts and builds, and would put a file parser in reach of untrusted input, so an older dictionary means an older package.
- The dictionary's releases are date tags. Since 2025 there has been one a year, at the end of January, following the General Specifications release ratified that month, and before that several a year, so a mid-year release can still carry an urgent change. Past releases added AIs, changed their flags, renamed and added linters, changed linter rules and code lists, and changed the file's own syntax. Each lands where a test sees it: the generator refuses a linter it does not know and the parser a syntax it does not read, and the counts of entries and AIs are pinned. The four packages stay in lockstep, so an update, which changes `FeatherQR.Gs1` alone, ships all four at a minor version (decided 2026-10-15). Leaving the lockstep would have meant changing `check_package_deps` and the release workflow for a release that comes about once a year.
- A release is noticed by `.github/workflows/gs1-dictionary.yaml`, which runs monthly, compares the newest date tag of the dictionary's repository with the release the generated table names, and opens one issue for each release that differs, whether that issue is later closed or not. A reminder each February after the January release would miss a mid-year one. GitHub disables a public repository's scheduled workflows after 60 days with no activity in the repository, and a disabled check notices nothing until it is enabled again.

### Generator entry points

- The generators get their GS1 entry points from this package (2026-10-13): `CreateGs1` writes the data as an element string with FNC1 in first position, and `CreateGs1DigitalLink` writes the data's Digital Link URI as plain text, each in the data, destination and size forms of `Create`, on Standard QR and rMQR. They are extension members with `Gs1QRCodeGenerator` and `Gs1RmQRCodeGenerator` as the named fallback, and they compose the data layer with the core's public `Create` and add nothing to it: the symbol is the one `Create` writes for the same string and options, which the tests hold module for module, and the core gained no member.
- `CreateGs1DigitalLink` has a second data form that takes the options and no stem. The stem is an optional parameter after the options, so for a bare `default` or a target-typed `new()` as the third argument the data form and the destination form both need a default filled in, and the destination, taken by value, is then the better match. The options-only form needs none and wins, which keeps for these members what the generators promise for `Create(text, level, default)`.
- The text is (AI) text when its first character is `(` and an element string otherwise, since an element string starts with an AI's digit. One rule serves both forms where a second set of members would have doubled the surface, and text that is neither, such as text with a leading blank, is refused as the element string it is read as. (AI) text gets its separators placed. An element string is checked and written as given, redundant separators included, because a caller who wrote it chose them and a reader tolerates them.
- Data that fails a check is a `Gs1FormatException`, a `FormatException` that carries the `Gs1Error`, and the error's place is in the text the caller passed: when a URI cannot carry data given as (AI) text, the builder's place in the element string is mapped back to the pair, and a missing primary key covers the whole text. The exception is not serializable, by decision: the serialization constructor is obsolete on the modern targets, and the one caller it would serve is .NET Framework code that lets the exception cross an application domain.
- `CreateGs1` sets the mode itself, so it takes `Fnc1` at its default or first position and refuses second position, which is another mode. `CreateGs1DigitalLink` refuses any FNC1 mode, because a scanner would read a URI under FNC1 as an element string. A wrong option is reported before wrong data, the order `Create` keeps between an option and content that does not fit, and the options are checked on the failing path alone, since on the other one `Create` checks them. The size forms throw for nothing but an option and answer `false` for data. A destination form reports a destination that is too small with the size form that sizes it, since `Create`'s own message names `Create`'s sizing member, which sizes the caller's text as plain text and so answers for another symbol.
- The destination and size forms allocate nothing while the shared pool holds an array of the size asked for (on .NET Framework it stops at 1,048,576 characters): the conversions run in stack buffers of 512 characters and in pooled buffers past that, an element string needs no element buffer since it is checked where it is, and the URI's buffer is sized from the lengths of the text and the stem (three characters a character of text, the percent escape) so that the URI is built in one pass.
- The data layer's checks take time in proportion to the length of the text, and the entry points run them on text of any length, with one exception: the two `TryGetRequiredBufferSizeGs1` forms answer `false` from the length alone for text no symbol holds (more than 7,089 characters of element string in Standard QR and 361 in rMQR, and twice that of (AI) text, which sheds at most half its length on the way), because there the answer does not depend on the data. Such text then costs neither the checks nor a pooled buffer of its length. The other members cannot do the same: a `Create` form owes the caller the data's error before the fit's, and a Digital Link URI can be far shorter than its text, since an AI repeated with one value is written once.
- rMQR is not a carrier GS1 lists (General Specifications 26.0), so the rMQR members say so in their documentation and refuse nothing. The layer does not see the symbol, and readers do read GS1 rMQR. Micro QR has no entry point, since it has no FNC1 mode and GS1 excludes it.
- The suite runs every bracketed and element string input of the GS1 corpus through the entry points and holds on each symbol `CreateGs1` writes with default options that it has FNC1 in first position, no ECI header and no Kanji segment, under both segmentations and in both symbologies.

### Not supported

| Out of scope | Why | Revisit when |
|---|---|---|
| Scanner transmission strings (a `]Q3` prefix, keyboard-wedge forms) | The decoder reports the FNC1 mode instead, and an AIM symbology identifier follows from the mode and the ECI (the FNC1 and GS1 row of the scope table in [qrcode-symbologies.md](qrcode-symbologies.md)) | A request for an AIM symbology identifier member |
| Data titles and non-HRI text (`GTIN`, `BEST BEFORE`) | They would add the titles to the table, and the General Specifications make them optional (4.14) | A caller's request |
| Compressed Digital Link URIs, resolvers and `linkType` | The legacy compression is frozen at Digital Link 1.1.4 and superseded by a separate EPC binary standard, and retail requires the uncompressed form. A compressed URI is refused as such | A caller's request to read compressed URIs |
| A switch that turns the pairing check off | Members that build run every check. Five of the 21 General Specifications examples in the corpus show an attribute without its key, as a second symbol on the item would, and they are refused | A caller who needs to build data split across carriers |
| A dictionary loaded at run time | It would decide what the library accepts and builds, and would put a file parser in reach of untrusted input. Of the implementations surveyed only the Syntax Engine loads one, and its linters are compiled code even then | None. An older dictionary is an older package |
| GS1 DataMatrix, GS1-128 and DataBar | This library does not draw them | A symbology added to the library |
| Print guidance (X-dimension, print grade) | GS1 sets it per application, the X-dimension in the symbol specification tables and the grade per ISO/IEC 15415. The README says only that the default quiet zone is GS1's | A caller's request |

A lead outside the scope: the scheme and host of a Digital Link URI are case-insensitive, so an uppercase stem would let Alphanumeric mode carry it under `Optimal`. It needs the Digital Link standard's view and phone readers checked first.

### Costs

- On a typical label, by the paired timing (the benchmark's three labels, retail, logistics and weighed, one call and one label a process, five rounds, the medians, Release, .NET 10, recorded 2026-10-15), the readers cost 0.14 to 0.24, 0.39 to 0.59 and 0.44 to 0.70 µs (`TryToHri`, `TryFromDigitalLink`, `TryRead`), `TryValidate` 0.26 to 0.42 µs, `TryFromHri` 0.35 to 0.56 µs and `TryToDigitalLink` 1.19 to 1.34 µs, the dearest since it validates and then re-splits the string to choose the path and order the query. `Gs1DataLayer` and `Gs1SymbolEncode` in the benchmark project run the same calls. CodeGlyphX's validator costs 0.43 to 0.79 µs on the same labels in the benchmark's run of 2026-10-15 and allocates 1,456 to 2,184 B.
- The entry points add the data layer's work to an encode and nothing else: by the same timing `CreateGs1` on the same labels costs 1.48 to 1.99 µs where `Create` on the element string costs 1.06 to 1.35 µs, and `CreateGs1DigitalLink` costs 2.97 to 3.47 µs where `Create` on the URI costs 1.31 to 1.54 µs, with nothing allocated.
- Valid data of 20,000 elements, in four shapes, is checked in 1.3 to 4.1 ms by `TryValidate`, built in 1.7 to 4.6 ms by `TryFromHri` and in 5.4 to 8.8 ms by `TryToDigitalLink`, where rules that scanned the text for each element took 3.7 to 15.4 s a call (the fastest of three calls, and one call of the old rules, Release, .NET 10.0.9, Ryzen 9 7950X3D, 2026-10-15).
- Three costs were left as they are. `TryToDigitalLink` scans the text once for each distinct AI it writes into the query, to write them in order, which the dictionary's AIs bound. An exclusion refused in (AI) text pays more than before the checks became linear, 1.25 times the old time on (AI) text of (02), (01), (11), (37) and (10), since the whole text fills the set before the first exclusion is asked. A refusal at the second element pays for clearing the set, 1.13 to 1.19 times the old time on .NET 8 and .NET Framework 4.8 by the paired timing, where on .NET 10 it takes 0.75 times. Leaving the set uncleared took back part of the difference, but the library keeps its stack buffers zero-initialized, as [standardqr-encoder.md](standardqr-encoder.md) decides for the encoder.

## Why

A plan that stopped at FNC1 would have missed retail, which uses Digital Link URIs in plain QR. Reading GS1 data needs the AI table as much as checking it does, because an element of predefined length carries no separator, so formatting a decoded symbol as `(AI)` text cannot work without lengths. Writing is where a caller goes wrong: an encoder that takes any element string cannot tell a missing separator from a long value, so it writes a wrong symbol with no error. That is why this layer ships in the same release as FNC1 encode, and FNC1 decode, which is safe without it, did not wait for either (decided 2026-10-10).

The table is generated because every implementation that checks GS1 data does so. libzint, BWIPP and CodeGlyphX generate their tables from the dictionary, and zxing-cpp keeps a hand-maintained, length-only table that cites an older release. A hand-maintained table drifts, and a generated one changes only when the pinned release does. A hand-written table was considered for the notice it might avoid, and it would avoid none: a transcription of the same file is the same derivative work, and re-sourcing from the General Specifications would move the code lists and the 34 linter rules to the standard's text while the tests still use the dictionary project's 5,656 vectors. In its own package the notice costs the core nothing (decided 2026-10-12).

A reader accepts AIs newer than its table, and a builder refuses them. The AI's own length follows from its first two digits (Table 7-5), and GS1 says the predefined lengths (Table 7-6) "will remain unchanged", so an unknown AI can be read by that length or up to the next separator, as the Syntax Engine reads it when it permits unknown AIs. When building, an unknown AI is more likely a typo than a new AI.

The pairing rules are checked per symbol although the dictionary defines them over all the carriers on an item. A per-symbol check can refuse data that is valid on the item, such as a QR with batch and expiry beside a linear barcode with the GTIN. The members that build follow the reference: the Syntax Engine, BWIPP and CodeGlyphX check pairings by default, and libzint does not. The refusals this costs are recorded with a revisit condition (Not supported, above).

The generators take `(AI)` text because the libraries that take an element string behind a flag let a missing separator through (ZXing.Net, go-qr, CodeGlyphX's Standard QR encoder), and the ones that take `(AI)` text are the ones a caller cannot misuse (libzint and zxing-cpp's writer through it, BWIPP, CodeGlyphX's rMQR encoder). The entry points run every check and set FNC1 themselves, so a caller needs to know nothing of the GS1 format and cannot forget the option (decided 2026-10-12, over composing the conversion with the FNC1 option on `Create`). The decoders gained no member. A writer owes the separators, so the encoder is where a GS1 entry prevents a wrong symbol. A reader owes only the mode. None of the libraries surveyed gives its decoder a GS1 entry (zxing-cpp formats HRI in a text mode, and the others return the mode and the element string), and `TryRead` on the data layer serves every decode entry point without multiplying with them.

## Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The entry type's name | `Gs1ElementString`, after the hub every member converts to or from. Every public type carries the `Gs1` prefix, as `Fnc1Mode` carries `Fnc1` | A type named `Gs1` was compiled against callers in four namespaces. It fails (CS0234, the simple name binds to the namespace) only for a caller inside another `FeatherQR` namespace, which is where this repository's tests and the Playground live and almost no consumer's code does. The longer name costs one word |
| `Try` forms only on the data layer | No throwing `FromHri` or `ToDigitalLink` | The generator entry points take `(AI)` text directly, so a throwing conversion had no caller a `Try` form does not serve |
| Sizing the span forms | An exact-length `TryGet…Length` twin for each, named after the member it sizes, beside a documented bound | The exact form leaves both choices to the caller: exactness from the twin, or a bound from the input alone. The decoders' `GetMaxDecodedLength` exists because their bound is not a function of the input, which is not the case here. Named after the output, two twins would collide, since two members produce an element string. The exact length costs a second pass over the input |
| The error | `Gs1Error`, a kind with an offset and a length, and `Gs1FormatException` from the one-line forms, derived from `FormatException` as `UriFormatException` is | A caller can point at the bad element, the one-line forms give the place too, and an existing `catch (FormatException)` still works. No new exception type would have forced callers who want the place onto the `Try` forms |
| `DictionaryRelease` | A static property, not a constant | It is read from the package in use rather than inlined into the caller at compile time |
| Repeated AI in a URI | Refused, equal values included, as the Syntax Engine refuses it | URI Syntax 1.7.0 says the last value wins (3), but the engine is GS1's reference and a reader that drops data in silence is the worse default. A last-wins rule was built first and dropped the same day |
| Two primary keys in one element string | The first in element-string order leads the URI | The Syntax Engine does the same |
| AIs the standard lists and the dictionary does not flag | Refused in a URI until the dictionary flags them ((7041), (8040) to (8043)) | The flags are the dictionary's to give, both dictionary-driven oracles refuse them, and the next release the table is regenerated from lifts them |
| The pairing checks in linear time | A set of the AIs present indexed by the AI's digits, first values in a table indexed by the AI's rank in the set, the old passes kept in the test project as `Gs1PairingReference` | A pattern names a range of numbers, not of table entries (`310n` is 3100 to 3109 where its entry is 3100 to 3105), so an index by entry would cost a search for each rule. Indexed by the AI, the table of first values would need a slot for each of the set's 11,100 numbers, and indexed by the entry about 18 KB of stack or a new generated table to number the 541 AIs. Passes of 32 AIs each with a small table cost 224 ns an element on text of 198 AIs that may stand together, against 85 ns for one pass (Release, .NET 10) |
| The tests' unknown AIs | One holder, `Gs1UnassignedAi`, with a test that fails when the pinned dictionary assigns one of them | A release can assign any of them, and the failure then lands in one place rather than in a dozen test rows |

## Lessons learned

### GS1 data

- A reference implementation's output shows its own dictionary release, not the standard. zxing-cpp's hand table and libzint's generated one are older than CodeGlyphX's, so a disagreement needs its release named before it is called a defect.
- The pairing rule, applied per symbol, refuses the General Specifications' own figures. Five of the 21 cases show an attribute without its key, as a second symbol on the same item would, and the engine refuses all five.
- "Fixed length" has two meanings in GS1 data. The table's format can be fixed ((8005) is N6) while the element string is not of predefined length ((8005) is not in Table 7-6), and a reader must take the separator's word over the format for the second kind, or a missing separator goes unreported.
- The engine's generator and parser disagree on (01)(235)(10). The parser accepts `/01/…/235/…?10=…`, and the generator strands (235) because it picks the first sequence with the most matches before asking what is left over. Preferring a sequence that leaves only data attributes behind makes the two directions agree, at one more pass over the elements.
- A reader that converts must keep the split. Reading a URI value as it is would let `/01/123` through, and the element string `01123` splits as (01) with a value cut short, so `TryRead` could fail after `TryFromDigitalLink` succeeded, with an offset into a string the caller never saw. Two value rules belong to reading for that reason, the predefined length and the control characters, and nothing else about a value.
- The standard does not say what a compressed URI looks like to a reader that does not decompress. The legacy compression is frozen and retail forbids it, so the kind is named by a heuristic on the final path segment (ten or more base64url characters with both letter cases), and only after no key was found, so no valid URI can hit it.
- Reading is not checking. `TryRead` gives (AI) text for an element string whose check digit is wrong, as a reader that shows what a symbol says should.
- No requisite of dictionary 2026-01-27 names its own AI, where 368 AIs are matched by an exclusion pattern of their own. The rule that an element is not its own requisite is kept from the old passes, and no text reaches it.

### API

- What decides the release is where a caller can go wrong. Reading GS1 data is safe without this layer. Writing it is not.
- A scope table's Out column reads as a decision. A hand-written table sat there as the investigation's recommendation, a later record called it rejected, and the maintainer had never been asked. A recommendation in a scope row needs the word, or a decision row of its own.
- An argument from the wrong axis can carry a decision row. The package question was first argued in kilobytes, since the core split had rejected a package for a saving in kilobytes, and the reason that decided it, the license, was listed nowhere.
- A namespace collision is narrower than "the type is hidden". The compile probe showed the simple name `Gs1` binding to the namespace only for callers inside another `FeatherQR` namespace.
- "No dependency" was a simplification that became an argument. The package needed no dependency only while every member worked on text. The costs a dependency brings, overload twins and a named fallback class for older compilers, had a precedent in the rendering package.
- An optional parameter after the options changes what a bare `default` selects. `Create(text, level, default)` reaches the options because they are its last parameter, so the form with a destination is the only one that needs a default filled in. One more optional parameter behind them makes both forms need one, and the tie goes to the by-value `Span<byte>`.
- The order of two errors is behavior. `Create` reports an option before content, and a layer that checks data first reverses that unless it asks for the option check on the path where `Create` never runs.
- A length can answer for a member only where the answer does not depend on the data. That is two of the fourteen entry points.
- Check a built value before the join, not after. Validating the joined element string and mapping every offset back would report a value that overflows a predefined-length AI as an unknown AI at the overflow, because the joined string re-splits there.

### Oracles and tests

- The reference's unit tests are the cheapest complete oracle a linter can have. 32 of the 34 linters needed no case of their own: the imported vectors enumerate the rule's edges, and the first run found the rules the specification text leaves open. A list linter's tests name every code of its range, so a test that compares the generated list with those verdicts needs no second transcription of ISO 3166 or ISO 4217.
- A join of bracketed text is not the element string the engine refused. Where the engine refused a value's length for a predefined AI, the join reparses into other elements and the validator rightly accepts them, so the comparison checks that the join reads back into the same AIs before it asserts anything.
- A fixture's kind names the mode its oracle was run in, not what the text is. One bracketed fixture holds an element string, and the entry points take it as one.
- A range entry is one line and many prefixes. The first test of Table 7-5 took each entry's first AI, missed that `91-99` is one line, and reported prefix 92 as unassigned.
- A tool's refusal of an empty surface bites a new package. The API listing and the documentation filter refuse an assembly with no public type, to stop a broken read from emptying a file, and a package with no public type yet reads as exactly that.
- A file derived from its twin needs the twin's tests in full. The rMQR members were generated from the Standard QR file and their tests written shorter, and both faults the first planted run missed were in the rMQR Digital Link size form.
- Members behind one signature are held by one test each. The level was held on some members and not others, the century on three of twelve, and the order of the FNC1 refusal and the data check on none, until one test of each held all fourteen.
- A sentence about what a fuzz test holds needs the shape of its inputs. One said no buffer sized from the text was too small, and no text it took was long enough for anything to be written into one.
- A fix is new code. Fifteen of the seventeen claims that stood in the second review round of the entry points, and all nine of the third, were about something the round before had added or rewritten: a handler, a branch, a member, a test, a check in a tool, a sentence.
- The layout of a set cannot be wrong in a way a text shows. Any layout that gives each AI its own bit behaves the same, so the faults planted on it were of another kind: bits that ignore the AI's length, a range one bit short, a range read in its first word only.

### Measuring

- A bound on the clock has to be measured on both sides in the build the suite runs in. The first bound was one second for 20,000 elements, and the new checks took 0.9 to 1.6 s for the URI in a Debug build beside the other GS1 classes, so the test runs apart from the other tests of its process, on 40,000 elements, with five seconds.
- A bound on the clock holds only for the shapes it runs. Every shape had the key every requisite names first and at most four AIs, so a requisite confirmed by a scan and a repeat check of 32 AIs a pass both passed it. A shape is needed for each place a scan could meet what it looks for late.
- A test that shows by the clock that slow code did not run stops showing it when the code gets fast. The test of the size forms held their answer from the length by the seconds the checks took, and it now reads the pool's rent events at each member's own capacity.
- A probe that runs several versions of a class in one process compiles the methods they share once, with one profile. Its readings of one version moved between processes, and a fix made on such a reading slowed `TryValidate` by 5 to 12 % when timed with a process for each version, so it was undone.
- A benchmark's setup has to check each call's answer. One row of the data layer's benchmark timed a refusal for two days: the element string read back from the retail URI has its elements in the URI's order and needs one separator more, so a buffer as long as the original was too short.
